comments.author: @JORGE-bg7vn
comments.text:
I'd like to add a new comment after the one I made yesterday.

I was thinking about how local people must feel after receiving the exciting news that a huge Cruise Ship is getting closer. At that moment, in their hearts, they imagine 3000 people suddenly walking through the island, bringing excitement, going to their restaurantes, enjoying the food they prepared for them,  buying colourful dresses or some souvenirs from the village market,  like a fantastic and happy party that, in a few hours, will change the lives of everybody but then... Bad news strikes, because the ship must continue its route because of the bad weather.

I assume that moment must be devastating for them, particularly because they know that the next chance could be in 2 or 3 weeks time and, even so, the bad weather can ruin their happiness again in a blink of an eye without mercy. 
Probably "endurance" must be a very important word in their dictionary.
Thanks for this beautiful video.

comments.author: @JORGE-bg7vn
comments.text:
Hi !  Nice video.

In 2011 we were in a 30 day cruise  (Hawaii. Bora Bora, Morea, Tahiti, Nukujiva,  etc). We couldn't get to Cook Island because of the bad weather. Unfortunately, those islands show the same story like other similar places. We were in Fanning Island (just a dot in the middle of nowhere) and they have the same problem.
I know that it sound hard, but from the nature point of view, they are NOT suitable places to live because just one huge storm can destroy everything (including the people). But they love their home and they do not want to leave. Anyway, time will tell although nature always has the last word.
By the way, I am watching this video from the Costa del Sol (south of Spain)
